title: KV shard-handoff and hybrid low-bit quantization field evaluation
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: run a small-scale, production-adjacent field evaluation of a hybrid low-bit KV compression strategy that combines FP8 for recently-written KV shards and INT4/INT8 for cold shards, while exercising continuous batching and our KV shard-handoff paths. Goals are to measure real-world quality impact, end-to-end latency (including on-the-fly dequantization), actual GPU memory savings across mixed workloads, and operational complexity for rollout.
updates: 2025-11-12: Kickoff — defined hypothesis and scope. Hypothesis: hybrid per-shard quantization yields >30% average GPU memory reduction with <2% generation-quality regression on our production prompt set when combined with prefix caching and smart shard eviction.

2025-11-14: Implemented per-shard metadata header to mark precision and version. Added APIs to the runtime for 'recompress_shard' and 'serve-from-compressed' flags. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4028.

2025-11-15: Baseline capture — snapshot of 72-hour traffic at 3 service replicas to create representative batching/seq-length distribution. Exported KV shard usage heatmap to internal dashboard (link below).

2025-11-17: Dry-run on staging with continuous batching enabled at low QPS. Observed a 28% median wall-clock GPU memory reduction when using FP8 for hot shards + INT8 for warm shards + INT4 for cold shards, but with occasional spike in per-request latency due to dequantize during shard handoff.

2025-11-18: Quality evaluation round 1 — ran generation regression harness on 1000 curated prompts including long-context summarization and multi-turn chat. Measured metric: relative log-prob shift and top-1 token delta. Observed average token-level disagreement 1.9% vs FP16 baseline; failures concentrated on long-context arithmetic and numeric copying tasks.

2025-11-19: Investigated high-latency handoffs — root cause: synchronous recompression/decompression performed inline on serving thread during shard fetch. Prototype async recompression worker implemented; initial results show 40% reduction in tail latency at cost of small CPU usage increase.

2025-11-20: Decided to proceed with limited field rollout to 5% of traffic using a conservative hybrid profile (FP8 hot, INT8 warm, keep cold as FP16 until next safety net). Added canary metrics and automatic rollback on quality drift >3% or latency P95 > 1.5x baseline.
findings_summary: Per-shard hybrid quantization can materially reduce GPU memory pressure in production-like workloads. FP8 for hot shards preserves most quality while giving the highest per-shard compression benefit; INT8 is a good tradeoff for warm shards. INT4 shows the largest memory wins but concentrated regressions on particular token types and brittle numeric tasks. Synchronous recompression on shard handoff is the primary contributor to tail latency spikes; moving recompression off hot serving threads reduces latency but introduces CPU/queueing tradeoffs.
numeric_results: Staging baseline (FP16 all shards): median GPU usage per replica 24.6 GB
Hybrid (FP8 hot / INT8 warm / INT4 cold): median GPU usage per replica 16.9 GB (~31% reduction)
Hybrid conservative (FP8 hot / INT8 warm / FP16 cold): median GPU usage per replica 18.2 GB (~26% reduction)
Quality: average token disagreement vs FP16: conservative hybrid 1.9%, aggressive hybrid 3.7%
Latency: synchronous recompress P95 increased by up to 2.3x; async offload reduced P95 regression to 1.15x
CPU: async recompress increased background CPU by ~9% on staging nodes
decisions: Adopt per-shard precision metadata; keep the format backwards-compatible with existing shard headers.
Default conservative profile for canary: FP8 hot, INT8 warm, FP16 cold. Aggressive profiles will be gated behind additional QA/regression tests.
Implement async recompression/decompression worker and a bounded queue to avoid unbounded memory/CPU usage during spikes.
Introduce a per-tenant safety net: if quality regression or latency exceeds thresholds, automatically revert that tenant's shards to FP16 and route to fallback model variant.
Add detailed signal tracking to Console: per-route quality delta, per-tenant memory savings, dequantization latency histogram, and recompress queue depth.
Create a migration tool to re-encode cold shards offline during low-load windows to avoid real-time recompress costs.
next_steps: 2025-11-21: Launch 5% canary for non-enterprise tenants (Miguel) — monitor quality delta, latency P95, and recompress queue depth for 72 hours
2025-11-22: Add targeted unit/regression tests for numeric copying and long-context summarization to the eval harness (Riley Chen)
2025-11-24: Run aggressive hybrid profile in synthetic load test to map failure modes (Ava)
2025-11-28: Conclude canary; prepare rollback/upgrade runbook and post-mortem template (Miguel + SRE)
2025-12-02: If canary success, schedule larger 25% rollout and begin work on permanent offline shard re-encoder (estimate 3 sprints)
